planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings after frost danger has passed in rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; this vigorous hybrid of B. aurea and B. versicolor fills out quickly and benefits from a sturdy support or staking once trumpets are large and heavy.

directions: 'Double White' bears ruffled, hose-in-hose double trumpets up to 10 inches long in loose pendant clusters, with soft gray hairs on the foliage that distinguish it from other candida-type hybrids. It is one of the most vigorous Brugmansia available, readily reaching small-tree size by its second season with heavy feeding and consistent moisture, and its sweet musky fragrance is strongest after dark. Where winters dip into the 20s expect dieback followed by spring resprouting from the base if mulched heavily; in colder zones overwinter container specimens indoors. All parts of the plant are highly toxic if ingested; site away from children and pets and wash hands after pruning or deadheading.

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings after frost in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; this compact, floriferous selection tolerates closer spacing than larger-growing angel's trumpets.

directions: 'Betty Marshall' is a compact, exceptionally free-flowering selection with single, pure white to cream trumpets that it produces in unusually heavy flushes relative to its more modest overall size. Its tidier habit makes it a good choice for smaller Gulf Coast beds or large containers where a full-size Brugmansia would quickly outgrow the space, and it carries the same strong evening fragrance typical of the genus. It has no frost tolerance and should be cut back and mulched heavily or brought under cover before freezing weather arrives. All parts of the plant are highly toxic if ingested; keep away from children and pets and wash hands after handling foliage or flowers.

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings after frost danger in rich, organic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; consistent moisture and regular feeding deepen the pink tone of the mature blooms.

directions: 'Ecuador Pink' opens its long single trumpets in a soft peach-apricot shade that gradually deepens to one of the richest pinks found in the genus as each flower matures, giving the shrub a two-tone look in full bloom. It flowers from spring through fall in warm climates and, like other Brugmansia versicolor selections, can grow into a substantial small tree where winters stay mild. In zone 9 protect from hard freezes with heavy mulch over the root zone or by overwintering containers indoors, since top growth has little cold tolerance. All parts of the plant are highly toxic if ingested; plant away from children's play areas and wash hands after pruning.

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings after frost in fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; give it room to spread, as this is a large, wide-growing selection.

directions: 'Shredded White Fantasy' is a novelty selection whose stark white, faintly green-tinged flowers separate into several distinctly spaced, ruffled petals ending in thin whisker-like points, giving each pendant bloom a torn or shredded look unlike the smooth-edged trumpets of typical angel's trumpets. It shares the heavy nighttime fragrance and vigorous, spreading growth habit common to candida-type hybrids, and flowers most heavily with rich soil, regular feeding, and consistent moisture. It has no cold tolerance, so mulch heavily after cutting back or move container plants under cover before frost. All parts of the plant are highly toxic if ingested; site away from children and pets and wash hands after handling.

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings after frost in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; this selection blooms while still young and small, so even first-year plants in containers typically flower.

directions: 'Inca Sun', bred from 'Insignis Orange' and 'Betty Marshall', is valued for flowering at an unusually young age and small size, often blooming continuously through the warm season rather than cycling through distinct flush-and-rest periods like most angel's trumpets. Its foot-long, single trumpets open pale yellow and warm to a peachy gold, releasing a strong sweet fragrance in the evening. It has no frost tolerance and should be cut back and heavily mulched or moved indoors before freezing weather. All parts of the plant are highly toxic if ingested; keep away from children and pets and wash hands after pruning or handling flowers.
